more.summary: Babies smell wonderful—at least to their parents. An international research team of Ilona Croy, Tomasz Frackowiak, Thomas Hummel and Agnieszka Sorokowska investigated why teenagers lose this special olfactory advantage and has now been awarded an Ig Nobel Prize for the research.

more.title: Startup ARR is less secure than ever, new research shows
more.author: Julie Bort
more.summary: The AI era has completely broken enterprise buying patterns, and startups haven't yet figured out how to navigate.

more.title: How a plant's refusal to self-pollinate could help India grow more of its own cooking oil
more.summary: Most people assume plants reproduce through whatever pollen happens to land on them. This is not true. A collaborative research initiative involving the Indian Institute of Technology Gandhinagar (IITGN) has mapped and functionally tested the genes that control a natural "self-rejection" system in two widely grown Indian oilseed crops, Brassica rapa (mustard) varieties toria and yellow sarson.

more.title: 'Empty nest' can trigger loneliness and loss in older parents, study finds
more.summary: Older parents can experience loneliness, emotional distress and a loss of purpose when their children leave home, according to a new pilot study by the University of Hertfordshire.

more.title: Utilities are racing to link up with fusion startups, with Realta Fusion the latest to benefit
more.author: Tim De Chant
more.summary: The grid has been straining under the weight of new AI data centers, and that has utilities courting fusion startups.

more.title: Perseverance rover watches Earth vanish behind Martian moon
more.summary: Earth and the Martian moon Phobos dance together in a series of images recently acquired by NASA's Perseverance Mars rover. Earth appears as a point of light in the Martian sky, disappearing behind the crescent of Phobos, the larger of Mars' two moons.

more.title: Live from ICM 2026: What Is Math For in the Age of AI?
more.author: Janna Levin and Steven Strogatz
more.summary: In this special live recording from the International Congress of Mathematicians in Philadelphia, July 2026, the central question discussed was what do mathematicians really value about doing mathematics in the first place? more.title: Your house may be a haven for wildlife. It's time we design homes with nature in mind
more.summary: Ever found a bare-nosed wombat napping under your house or heard a possum thumping around in your attic?

more.title: Ancient “living fossils” may reveal how complex life began
more.summary: A newly discovered microbe living inside ancient stromatolite communities may offer a rare look at how complex life first emerged. Researchers captured the first direct images of an Asgard archaeon physically connected to a bacterium, with the two microbes appearing to exchange nutrients and other compounds. Scientists think similar partnerships billions of years ago may have helped produce the first complex cells.

more.title: France recorded 'hottest summer ever': Environment minister
more.summary: France experienced its hottest summer on record in 2026, marked by heat waves, drought and massive wildfires, the environment minister said Thursday.

more.title: Scientists just overturned a century-old physics assumption
more.summary: Scientists at Carnegie Mellon University have discovered an unexpected form of the Hall effect, overturning the long-held assumption that this electrical response only appears when a magnetic field points perpendicular to a material. Beyond expanding a century-old principle of physics, the finding could eventually lead to simpler magnetic sensors for electronics, transportation, and medical technologies.

more.title: Bats carry dangerous viruses without getting sick. This may be why
more.summary: Scientists discovered that more than 500 species of vesper bats possess two separate sets of antibody genes, an immune arrangement never before found in mammals. The surprising system could help explain how bats tolerate so many viruses without becoming seriously ill.

more.title: How El Nino is choking the Panama Canal
more.summary: The Panama Canal will restrict the number of vessels transiting the crucial waterway from Friday for only the second time because of drought caused by the El Niño climate phenomenon.

more.title: Tiny fossils reveal big insights about ant ancestors
more.summary: Two tiny ant fossils recovered in southern Saskatchewan are helping scientists better understand the evolutionary history of modern ants. Ant fossils dating from 72–56 million years ago are rare. What happened to insects such as ants during this period that saw a mass extinction wipe out all non-bird dinosaurs? How did that event reshape their world?

more.title: How an unassuming wildflower thrives in salt-laden air that kills other plants
more.summary: On the windswept coasts of Oregon and California lives an unassuming little plant that can withstand salty blasts that kill its inland counterparts. It's called the yellow monkeyflower. Now, researchers are beginning to understand how it manages to thrive in conditions that leave other plants burned, brown and withered.
